title: Insights from Snorkel AI running Azure AI Infrastructure: Humza Iqbal and Lachlan Ainley
talk_summary: A Snorkel AI researcher and a Microsoft host describe Snorkel's data-development research and their experience running distributed fine-tuning on Azure GPU VMs. The transferable content is mostly infrastructure hygiene: right-sizing node counts to batch size, co-locating data and compute, watching GPU utilization, and comparing cost-per-work across GPU generations.

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat low accelerator utilization as the primary symptom and branch diagnosis: multi-node low utilization points to networking/gradient sync, single-node low utilization points to data loading.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you see your GPU utilization being low you know don't be afraid to look into why

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep training data and nodes in the same region and use a shared network filesystem so reads aren't a cross-region bottleneck.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want to make sure all of our data and nodes are close together

takeaways.what_they_do: They pick node counts to hit a target batch size, avoiding both too-large batches and underutilized nodes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want enough nodes to have a certain batch size but we also didn't want too many

takeaways.what_they_do: They compared equal-cost configurations (2 H100s vs 4 A100s) on the same fixed batch sizes and measured training and inference throughput per dollar.
takeaways.numbers: 2 H100s beat 4 A100s at equal cost on both training and inference

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue general benchmarks don't predict domain performance and build per-domain benchmarks, including long-context tests beyond needle-in-a-haystack.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for specific Industries you need specific benchmarks

takeaways.technique: Flexible on/off capacity over long periods
takeaways.what_they_do: They rejected fixed-duration compute commitments because experiments need variable node counts over months.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we wanted something where we could go on and off for a longer period of time
